title: A flat finite-presentation surjective cover makes the diagonal representable

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the statement

standard_prerequisites.name: Representable diagonal criterion
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the claim to representability of T1 x_X T2 by an algebraic space for representable T1, T2.

standard_prerequisites.name: Setoid fibre product is a stack
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies T1 x_X T2 as a stack in setoids, hence a sheaf F.

standard_prerequisites.name: Bootstrap theorem
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the representability of T1' x_U T2' -> F into algebraicity of F.

core_obligations: Identify T1 x_X T2 with a stack in setoids and its sheaf F.
Form T_i' = U x_X T_i, represented by algebraic spaces T_i', and place the four squares of the 3D diagram, checking which faces are 2-fibre products.
Extract that T1' x_U T2' -> T1 x_X T2 is the base change of U -> X and conclude flat/lfp/surjective transfer via the algebraic-stacks lemmas, then apply Bootstrap.
proof_roadmap: Write the 3D commutative diagram, verify the four named faces are 2-fibre products, deduce the displayed square is a 2-fibre square, transfer the four properties by base change, and close with the Bootstrap theorem.
difficulty_reason: The 3D cube bookkeeping (identifying four 2-fibre-product faces among eight) is the substance; the closing transfer is by named lemmas.
